So today I caught myself doing the thing again. I had the long run on the schedule, sixty minutes at the higher pace I've been working on. And around minute eighteen, my legs started feeling that specific kind of heavy where it's not pain, it's just the system telling you it's costing more than usual. And I noticed my brain immediately started building the case for cutting it short. "You ate late last night." "You didn't sleep great." "You can do the rest tomorrow as a brick session." All of it sounded reasonable. None of it was true. The truth was simply that the body was registering effort, exactly the kind of effort the workout was designed to apply, and my mind was negotiating to escape it. So I went back to the cookie jar — the specific one from January, the trail run when I bonked at kilometer eight and still finished. I held that memory for about thirty seconds, the texture of it, the feeling of getting up from the side of the path and the surprise that my legs still worked. And then I just kept running. The interesting thing is that the heaviness didn't go away. It actually got worse for another ten minutes. But the mental case for stopping dissolved. The negotiation closed. I want to remember this: the cookie jar isn't there to make the discomfort smaller, it's there to make the urge to escape it less convincing. The body still has to do the work. The mind just stops being your opponent.
